name: Idaho
text: Federal law sets the national baseline; see the national record for United States. House Bill 752, signed by Governor Brad Little and effective 1 July 2026, makes it a crime for a transgender person to use a restroom or changing room that does not match the sex assigned at birth. It reaches government buildings and public-facing private businesses, including gas stations, restaurants, entertainment venues and hospitals. A first offence is a misdemeanour carrying up to one year in jail. The ACLU of Idaho filed suit on 30 April 2026 on due-process, equal-protection and privacy grounds, arguing the law targets no criminal conduct; six transgender Idahoans are plaintiffs in the challenge, brought before the effect date. According to the ACLU, Idaho's is the only state law extending bathroom criminalisation to private businesses, and it carries steeper penalties than other states' bans.

name: Louisiana
text: The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. In August 2026 a mob beat transgender couple Aurora Rush and Shae Sanders over restroom use at Cypress Black Bayou Park in Benton. Sanders has a pre-existing spinal injury and Rush suffered a concussion and blood pooling, and both were charged with disturbing the peace. The sheriff's office recorded no arrest of any attacker that day, and a plea deal had not been signed. Rush was denied hospital care, taken to a men's jail, held in a men's facility and searched by a male guard even though her driver's licence carries a female marker, which did not determine housing or search procedure. In the same period Benton voted one of the country's most severe anti-trans restroom ordinances. Gender-marker changes require surgical proof: a driver's licence change requires a physician-signed statement confirming successful sex reassignment surgery, and a new birth certificate requires a certified court order confirming surgical gender change with proof of a diagnosis recorded as transsexual or pseudo-hermaphrodite and of anatomical change. Louisiana's 1997 hate-crime statute provides penalty enhancements for offences motivated by sexual orientation or perceived sexual orientation but does not cover gender identity. Gender-affirming care for minors is banned, after the Legislature overrode the governor's June 2023 veto in July 2023 and the ban on puberty blockers, hormones and surgery took effect on 1 January 2024. Marriage is recognised after the 2015 invalidation of the state's 2004 constitutional ban on marriage and civil unions and its 1988 and 1999 Civil Code provisions, with full joint adoption and parental rights following the 2014 Costanza v. Caldwell ruling granting the state's first adoption by a same-sex couple. The unenforceable sodomy statute remains, carrying up to five years' imprisonment, a $2,000 fine and sex-offender registration, after a repeal bill failed 66-27 in April 2014. Louisiana has no state law prohibiting gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing or public accommodations. The Movement Advancement Project scores gender-identity policy at -8.75 out of 25 and overall policy at -8.75 out of 47 as of 12 October 2026. New Orleans and Shreveport prohibit gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations, while Alexandria, Baton Rouge, Lafayette, Lake Charles and Jefferson Parish extend protection only to public employees.

name: Texas
text: Federal employment, marriage and ID rules apply in Texas. The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Texas Women's Privacy Act (SB 8), signed by Governor Greg Abbott on 22 September 2025, effective 4 December 2025, limits restrooms to birth-certificate sex in public schools, universities, prisons and Texas government buildings; $25,000 fine for first violation and $125,000 for subsequent violations. Companion statute covers prisons only for restroom use, not cell/housing placement. On 6 December 2025 Department of Public Safety troopers checked ID at women's restrooms outside state Capitol in Austin, admitting trans women holding female ID markers; protests followed, Austin City Council moved to circumvent intent. On 27 April 2026 Attorney General Ken Paxton filed second complaint escalating Austin Independent School District bathroom-policy investigation with records demand after tip-line complaint, first inquiry into a school district under the law. July 2026 national assessment puts Texas in top 'Do Not Travel' tier for adult trans travellers alongside Florida, Idaho and Kansas. House Bill 229, Women's Bill of Rights, passed May 2025, signed June 2025, effective September 2025, defines female as one who can biologically produce ova and male as one who can biologically fertilize ova, requires binary selection with no third-gender recognition for disorders of sex development across gendered state laws, bans sex change on Texas driver's licences and birth certificates. Before, birth-certificate change needed court order referencing WPATH; on 30 January 2025 Abbott directed agencies to recognise only two genders. Gender-affirming care for minors banned since Senate Bill 14, signed June 2023, after February 2022 opinion calling it child abuse. Texas has no statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination law for employment, housing, public accommodations or insurance as of 2021, although Texas courts recognised federal employment protections in March 2021 and several cities prohibit such discrimination. Its hate-crime statute enhances penalties for sexual-orientation-motivated crimes but not gender identity, with rare prosecutions. Vanessa Lynn Gibson, transgender woman in Texas Department of Criminal Justice custody diagnosed with gender dysphoria, was denied gender-confirmation surgery per agency treatment policy excluding it. In Gibson v. Collier district court denied state immunity defences but rejected her Eighth Amendment claim, and Fifth Circuit affirmed dismissal as permissible medical choice, Judge Barksdale dissenting on summary-judgement procedure. Same-sex marriage has been licensed in Texas since 26 June 2015. No statewide domestic-partnership recognition for same-sex or opposite-sex couples, though Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, El Paso, Houston and San Antonio provide health insurance to domestic partners of city workers, and April 2013 attorney general opinion held state constitution bars political-subdivision benefits based on domestic-partnership status.

name: Kansas
text: Federal protections and restrictions apply nationwide. The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Kansas Senate Bill 244 was enacted on 26 February 2026 when the Legislature overrode Governor Laura Kelly's veto, and it took effect immediately. The law confines transgender people to sex-segregated facilities matching sex assigned at birth in publicly owned buildings, including schools, universities, airports and government offices. It creates civil and criminal penalties of up to $1,000 for using a non-matching facility and authorises bounty-style lawsuits of at least $1,000 by any private person who claims to have shared a bathroom with a transgender person. The same law bars updating of driver's licences and state identification cards and invalidates existing licences whose gender marker is inconsistent with sex assigned at birth. The Kansas Department of Revenue has been mailing written notice, and many holders have already been told their licence is now invalid. Reissue is at the holder's expense with no grace period, and surrender letters warn of additional penalties for driving without a valid credential. Two transgender men filed Doe v. State of Kansas in Douglas County District Court within days of enactment, represented by the ACLU and Ballard Spahr, citing fear of violence under the facility-restriction and identification-invalidation provisions. Senate Bill 180 was enacted in April 2023 by veto override, defined biological sex in state law and barred agencies from recognising genders beyond sex assigned at birth. The attorney general then directed that new or updated driver's licences and birth certificates reflect only original sex at birth. A temporary restraining order barred gender-marker changes, the Kansas Court of Appeals reversed unanimously on 13 June 2025 for lack of evidence of irreparable harm to law-enforcement identification, and in October 2025 the Kansas Supreme Court rejected an appeal, allowing the Department of Revenue to continue the changes. Kansas law has prohibited discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing and public accommodations since 2020, following Bostock v. Clayton County and Kansas Human Rights Commission action in August 2020 covering businesses with four or more employees. The state hate-crime law provides penalty enhancements for crimes motivated by sexual orientation but does not cover gender identity. Marriage for same-sex couples became available after U.S. District Judge Daniel D. Crabtree ruled the state ban unconstitutional on 4 November 2014, effective 12 November 2014, and became fully legal under Obergefell v. Hodges on 26 June 2015, with all judicial districts issuing licences by the end of that month. Consensual same-sex sexual activity is legal under Lawrence v. Texas (2003), though the Legislature has not repealed its same-sex-only sodomy provisions carrying historic penalties of six months in jail and/or $1,000.

name: Oklahoma
text: Oklahoma is a state within the United States, so a visitor stands under the national framework recorded in the parent country's dossier. Within that framework, Oklahoma's own statutes and executive acts restrict a transgender visitor's use of facilities, documents, care and sport more narrowly than the national baseline. The Movement Advancement Project's national tracker, current to 25 March 2026, lists Oklahoma among states banning transgender people from bathrooms and facilities matching their gender identity in K-12 schools, with enactments in 2022 and again in 2025. Senate Bill 615, signed in May 2022, requires transgender students and staff to use school bathrooms, changing rooms and similar facilities according to sex assigned at birth as stated on an original birth certificate rather than gender identity. That statute is associated with the 2024 death of 16-year-old non-binary student Nex Benedict, who was beaten in a school bathroom shortly before dying. Facility and role definitions at state level were widened by an executive order Governor Kevin Stitt signed on 1 August 2023, requiring state agencies to define female, woman, girl and mother as a person whose biological reproductive system is designed to produce ova and male, man, boy and father as a person whose system is designed to fertilise ova, based on sex assigned at birth. The order applies to state and legal purposes including bathrooms and changing rooms in state-owned facilities, sports, domestic violence shelters, rape crisis centres, incarceration and statistics collection, which restricts legal recognition of transgender people for state agency purposes. Birth certificates are the sharpest document exposure. Oklahoma recognised a non-binary birth-certificate option from October 2021 under Kit Vivien Loreleid v. Oklahoma State Department of Health, but in November 2021 Governor Stitt ordered the health department to block any gender-marker changes, and in April 2022 Senate Bill 1100 limited birth certificates to male or female only, banning other markers with immediate effect. House Bill 1225, which requires a male or female designation on Oklahoma birth certificates and prohibits changes with very little exception, passed its most recent vote 70-17 and on 6 May 2026 was headed to Governor Stitt's desk, still pending his signature. Its authors said it is designed to strengthen the existing law being challenged in federal court by transgender plaintiffs including a Tulsa resident, Rowan Fowler; the state Attorney General's office confirmed the bill clarifies that Oklahoma never permitted gender-marker changes, while critics called it further discrimination. In October 2026 the Oklahoma Supreme Court ruled retroactively that changing a birth-certificate gender marker was never legal, even to correct an error made for a cisgender person. Transgender Oklahomans could previously change driver's licences on a notarised physician statement of permanent and irreversible transition; the source does not describe the operative licensing practice after the 2021 and 2022 birth-certificate restrictions, and equality-map research shows conditions for changing a gender marker on a licence or birth certificate differ state by state. Sport is closed to transgender girls and women in public education. In March 2022 Governor Stitt signed a law barring transgender women and girls from women's and girls' athletic teams at public schools and universities, and in 2022 he signed S.B. 2 prohibiting transgender students from playing school sports consistent with their gender identity and excluding all transgender girls from school athletics. Gender-affirming care is restricted on several fronts. An October 2022 law bars government funding to Oklahoma hospitals providing any gender transition services to minors. An April 2023 law, signed in May 2023, explicitly bans any gender-affirming healthcare practice on minors, making Oklahoma the 16th state with such a restriction, and a judge declined to block it in October 2023. Senate Bill 904, passed at the end of the 2026 session (77-14 in the House, 39-8 in the Senate) and signed on 14 May 2026 with immediate effect, bars use of public funds, Oklahoma Medicaid (SoonerCare) coverage or reimbursement, and state-owned properties and healthcare facilities for gender-affirming surgeries, puberty blockers, cross-sex hormones and other medications that delay puberty or develop secondary sex characteristics where they affirm a gender identity different from sex assigned at birth, for minors and adults alike. Intentional violations by state employees are a criminal misdemeanour; patients face no penalties. The ban exempts mental health counselling, anxiety and depression medication, precocious puberty treatment, intersex care, treatment of complications from prior gender-affirming care, and emergency treatment to prevent death or major impairment, leaving gender-affirming medical care available only at privately owned facilities paid by private insurance or out of pocket, without Medicaid. A February 2023 House-passed bill to bar publicly funded entities from providing or permitting gender-affirming care to transgender people of any age and to ban insurance coverage did not pass the Senate and did not become law. State statutes provide no discrimination protection on the basis of gender identity. Norman prohibits discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations on gender identity and sexual orientation, while Edmond, Oklahoma City and Tulsa prohibit it only for public city employment. Oklahoma is an at-will employment state, permitting dismissal without a stated reason. State hate-crime law does not cover gender identity, so a bias-motivated assault against a transgender person is prosecuted without the state enhancement. Violence directed at trans and gender-nonconforming minors is documented: in 2018 a school in Achille closed for days after a 12-year-old transgender student received death threats, including threats of mutilation, whipping and castration, from classmates' parents. An advocacy legal-risk assessment, the Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map published in July 2026, assigns Oklahoma a per-state traveller risk grade alongside the other states; that edition added a fourth 'Do Not Travel' state and tracked changes to its 'Worst Laws Passed' tier, but the source does not state Oklahoma's specific grade. Relationship recognition is settled in the opposite direction. Same-sex marriage and adoption by same-sex couples have been permitted in Oklahoma since October 2014, after voters approved Question 711 on 2 November 2004 banning same-sex marriage and its legal incidents, Judge Terence C. Kern declared it unconstitutional on 14 January 2014 in Bishop v. United States, the Tenth Circuit upheld that ruling on 18 July 2014, and the U.S. Supreme Court denied appeal on 6 October 2014. Oklahoma permits adoption by a couple or unmarried adult without regard to sexual orientation, and in August 2007 the Tenth Circuit in Finstuen v. Crutcher ordered the state to recognise a same-sex couple's adoption and issue a revised birth certificate. State law nevertheless allows agencies to refuse placements that violate their written religious or moral convictions. Lesbian couples can access fertility treatment and IVF, with state law recognising a married non-genetic, non-gestational mother as a legal parent, although a 2023 district judge stripped such a wife's rights in favour of a sperm donor where she was absent from the donor contract and had not adopted.

name: Indiana
text: Indiana is subject to United States federal rules, and the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Indiana's Bureau of Motor Vehicles ban on gender-marker changes to driver's licences and state ID cards took effect on 1 February 2026. It ended the route through a court-ordered gender change or a physician's statement. It completed an administrative rule change the bureau initiated. LGBTQ advocates who testified against it said it would forcibly out transgender and nonbinary residents whose documents no longer match how they present. The ACLU has challenged the policy in court. Governor Mike Braun's March 2025 executive order defining sex solely as assigned sex at birth directed the Indiana Department of Health to stop updating gender markers, and the bureau's 2026 rule extended that prohibition to licences and ID cards. Birth-certificate changes had been available by court order from 2014 until 2025. In May 2023 the Indiana Supreme Court declined in split votes to hear two cases by transgender girls seeking amended birth certificates, leaving appellate rulings standing that trial courts have no authority to grant a change unless the General Assembly codifies it. One case involved a nine-year-old transgender girl whose birth certificate's male designation her school used to restrict bathroom access. Indiana issued an X marker between March 2019 and January 2020 on an amended birth certificate or a physician's statement confirming permanent gender change. The bureau withdrew it after a public hearing, and a March 2020 attorney general opinion held only the General Assembly could authorise nonbinary designations. As of April 2026, Indiana law places no restriction on transgender people using restrooms matching gender identity, and Indianapolis and Bloomington ordinances expressly protect that use. Proposals to criminalise it have died in committee since 2021, and in August 2023 a Seventh Circuit decision upheld a preliminary injunction barring schools from limiting a transgender student's bathroom use while litigation continued. Senate Bill 182 passed the Indiana Senate 37-8 on 27 January 2026 on a party-line vote and went to the House. It would define sex and gender by reproductive biology at birth, permanently bar birth certificate amendments, require public K-12 schools and state universities to designate multi-person restrooms, locker rooms and changing areas for males or females as assigned at birth only, and confine prison housing to birth sex placement. Author Senator Liz Brown of Fort Wayne said it protects women's private spaces. Opponents including GenderNexus warned a provision allowing anyone directly or indirectly injured to sue a school would encourage harassment-style enforcement. The bill received no House hearing and is not law. Gender-affirming care for minors is barred. Senate Bill 480, passed and signed in 2023 under an emergency clause, prohibits physicians from providing gender-transition procedures to anyone under 18 or aiding such care, with a phase-out for existing patients. It was enjoined on 16 June 2023, took effect on 27 February 2024 after a stay, and was upheld in November 2024. The ban covers surgery, puberty blockers and hormone therapy. A trans visitor under 18 cannot obtain that care in Indiana. Indiana's hate-crimes law, enacted in April 2019, allows harsher sentences where an offence was motivated by perceived or actual characteristics, gender identity among them. It creates an aggravating circumstance rather than a standalone offence. The state had tracked bias crimes without sentencing enhancement from 2003 until then.

name: North Dakota
text: North Dakota stands under the United States national framework for passports, entry screening and federal identity documents. The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. A national anti-trans legal-risk assessment dated July 2026, built from five years of daily legislative tracking and a rubric scoring the most severe bills, lists North Dakota among the worst states for legislation targeting transgender adults, and among the states that prohibit any change to birth certificates. The assessment states that this prohibition forces transgender people to disclose their status when presenting documents. Birth-certificate gender markers are effectively closed. The Movement Advancement Project's identity-document tracker records that North Dakota's 2023 law bans all gender-marker changes on birth certificates with a narrow exception for individuals who have had genital surgery, a stricter and more explicit surgical requirement than in many other states, and marks North Dakota a negative-law state. The regulations accompanying the 2023 statute were rejected, leaving in place a 2008 regulation restricting changes to those who have undergone a sex conversion operation. Driver's licences and state ID cards follow a separate and lower threshold: the Department of Transportation updates the gender marker on receipt of a physician or therapist letter stating that the applicant has completed a permanent gender role transition. North Dakota statutes do not explicitly prohibit discrimination on the basis of gender identity. City-level protections exist in Grand Forks for city employees and applicants and in rental housing from 2013. An April 2021 state law allows student groups at colleges, universities and high schools to discriminate against LGBT students. Providing gender-affirming care to minors is illegal under a bill passed by a veto-proof majority on 5 April 2023. Two bills signed into law in April 2023 ban individuals assigned male at birth from female sports and athletics in schools and in higher education respectively. A 2021 bill to the same effect passed the House 69 to 25 and the Senate 27 to 20 but was vetoed by Governor Doug Burgum on 21 April 2021. An April 2023 law, effective 1 July, explicitly allows restriction of transgender individuals' public bathroom usage in many state-run facilities. HB 1522 (2023), an act relating to preferred pronouns and accommodations to a transgender student, carried a penalty provision and an emergency clause, was signed by the governor, and had its last official action filed with the Secretary of State on 9 May 2023. The corresponding May 2023 law, effective 1 July, forbids schools and government entities from requiring or prohibiting preferred pronoun use and requires disclosure of transgender students to parents in state-run schools. A March 2023 bill requiring parental and administrative approval for preferred pronoun use in state-run schools and classrooms had been vetoed. North Dakota's hate-crime law does not cover gender identity. A June 2021 committee regulation bans conversion therapy by social workers, psychologists and counsellors. Prior state constitutional and statutory restriction limited marriage to one man and one woman, and proceedings in Ramsay v. Dalrymple were suspended in January 2015. The Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians legalised same-sex marriage on its reservation by 6 to 2 in August 2020.

name: South Dakota
text: Federal employment and hate-crime protections provide limited backstop. The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. South Dakota restricts transgender use of bathrooms, locker rooms and changing areas matching gender identity in public schools and state-owned buildings under House Bill 1259, signed by Governor Larry Rhoden on 20 March 2025 and announced the following day. The law took effect on 1 July 2025 and passed the state House 49-21. Its scope covers state-run facilities, primarily K-12 schools and state colleges, including off-campus activities. It is the first facilities restriction of its kind enacted in the state, after comparable bills failed in 2016, 2017, twice in 2018 and in 2022. Its reasonable accommodation clause and floor debate raised the prospect that incarcerated transgender people would be placed in solitary confinement to comply. No South Dakota statute prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing or public accommodations, and the state hate-crime law does not cover gender identity. On 5 March 2026 the South Dakota Supreme Court ruled a transgender person cannot amend the sex designation on a South Dakota birth certificate to reflect gender identity, affirming denial of Sigrid Nielsen's September 2024 petition to change the marker from male to female and holding a change is permitted only to correct an error made at birth. Legal gender change on a driver's licence or state ID remains available by court order or physician affidavit confirming sex reassignment surgery, and on a birth certificate by court order, photo ID, application and fee. Gender-affirming care for people under 18 is banned under House Bill 1080, passed in February 2023 and signed on 13 February 2023. Prior puberty-blocker or hormone treatment had to be systematically reduced, ending no later than 31 December 2023, and affected people may sue until age 25 or within three years of discovering an injury. An advocacy legal-risk assessment published in July 2026 lists South Dakota among the worst states for legislation targeting transgender adults, drawing on five years of daily legislative tracking and a rubric for the most severe bills. On 16 December 2022 South Dakota terminated The Transformation Project's $136,000 federally funded Community Health Worker contract for LGBTQ+ and transgender community health in Sioux Falls. To settle the discrimination lawsuit, Health Secretary Melissa Magstadt issued an apology letter on 17 January 2024 acknowledging termination and differential treatment compared with other Community Health Worker contractors and affirming equal treatment regardless of race, colour, national origin, religion, disability, age or sex. The state paid $300,000 covering attorney fees, committed not to discriminate against the Project in violation of state or federal law in any services, programmes or activities, and allowed retention of community health worker Jack Fonder.

name: West Virginia
text: See the national record for United States for the federal layer. Senate Bill 456, the Riley Gaines Act, signed by Governor Patrick Morrisey on 12 March 2025 after passing Senate on 3 March and House on 6 March, defines woman as adult human of female sex and man as adult human of male sex with no category beyond male and female, after language requiring genital examination was struck. Governor said bathrooms, locker rooms, domestic violence shelters and rape crisis centres should be kept private for women only. It covers locker rooms, bathrooms, rape crisis centres, dormitories and prisons and is listed in Movement Advancement Project map. 27 August 2026 assessment places West Virginia in Worst States group, one tier below the four states rated Do Not Travel, within Worst Policies In Effect. Birth certificate change needs Birth Certificate Request Form with court order and fees to Vital Registration; licence or ID needs Gender Designation Form signed by licensed physician, no surgery or sterilisation required. In July 2020 West Virginia Supreme Court upheld refusal even after reassignment surgery. House Bill 3293, passed March 2021 effective 1 July 2021, defines male and female solely on reproductive biology and genetics at birth for teams; West Virginia v. B. P. J. in April 2024 held unconstitutional, Supreme Court in July 2025 agreed to hear case. March 2023 law effective 1 January 2024 bans puberty blockers, hormone therapy and surgery except severe dysphoria diagnosed by at least two physicians. 1997 Medicaid ban on sexual reassignment surgery ruled unconstitutional in August 2022, overturned in 2026 holding refusing funding is not irrational; Anderson v. Crouch on adult exclusion argued 9 December 2025, unresolved. April 2025 bill passed both houses, awaited gubernatorial action, requiring teachers and principals to immediately out transgender, non-binary and intersex students to parents and guardians. Statutes provide no discrimination protection on gender identity except statewide employment protection from federal Bostock Title VII, while fifteen cities bar gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations plus county and city employee protections in Kanawha County, Buckhannon and Elkins. House Bill 3042, passed 27 and 28 February 2023, is Religious Freedom Restoration Act letting person or corporation claim exemption where state or local law burdens religious belief, permitting denial of business service, housing and government service on gender identity, with qualified immunity. On 26 March 2025 state Senate approved by 25 to 8 bill to nullify all city and county LGBTQ anti-discrimination ordinances, awaiting House vote. Marriage for couples state would class as same-sex recognised since 9 October 2014, when Attorney General Patrick Morrisey ceased defending ban and Governor Earl Ray Tomblin directed agencies to comply federally, despite unrepealed statute defining marriage as between man and woman.

name: Arkansas
text: Under United States federal rules; the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Act 619 of 11 April 2023 and law signed 21 March 2023 restrict transgender students' use of school bathrooms matching gender identity, making Arkansas the fourth such state, amended and extended in 2025, with HB 1156 as 2023 K-12 facility ban extended in 2025. Act 619 creates a misdemeanour for transgender use of public bathrooms, locker rooms or changing facilities where a minor is present, dependent on intent of arousing or gratifying sexual desire. July 2026 map places Arkansas in 'The Worst States', one tier below 'Do Not Travel' for Florida, Idaho, Kansas and Texas. Arkansas was the first state, in 2021, to ban gender-affirming healthcare for trans minors after override of governor's veto, via HB 1570 banning puberty blockers, hormone therapy and surgery for under-18s, vetoed on 5 April 2021 but overridden on 6 April 2021, blocked then struck down on 20 June 2023 by Judge James M. Moody Jr., before Eighth Circuit overturned it on 12 August 2025 allowing enforcement citing Skrmetti, with 2021 ban litigation continuing enjoined for 'irreparable harm'. Senate Bill 256 passed 34-0 in Senate and 92-0 in House on 19 February 1981 requiring court order verifying sex reassignment surgery and name change for birth amendment since 1981. X was available from December 2010, rescinded in March 2024 for driver's licences. Little Rock, Conway, Hot Springs, North Little Rock and Pulaski County bar public-employment discrimination; Eureka Springs and Fayetteville ordinances unenforced under Intrastate Commerce Improvement Act; Fayetteville ordinance struck down in February 2017. Arkansas has no hate-crime penalty-enhancement statute; civil remedy for intimidation, harassment, violence or property damage covers only racial, religious or ethnic animosity, not gender identity; April 2021 hate-crimes law signed effective immediately excludes sexual orientation or gender identity explicitly or implicitly. SB 289 signed 26 March by Governor Asa Hutchinson and effective immediately lets medical practitioners cite religious beliefs to deny healthcare to LGBT patients. In March 2021 Legislature passed transgender-athlete ban signed 25 March and effective immediately, enacted 25 March 2021 per ESPN, prohibiting transgender women and girls from competing on school sports teams consistent with gender identity across K-12 and collegiate sports, allowing a student or school claiming harm to sue a school for violation. In March 2023 Legislature passed gender-affirming litigation bill signed 13 March 2023 by Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders, allowing recipients of such care as minors to sue providers 15 years after turning 18, versus two years for other care.

name: Ohio
text: Federal law applies in Ohio, the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Erin In The Morning's July 2026 map places Ohio in "The Worst States," sixteen states forming the second-highest tier beneath the four graded "Do Not Travel," under "Worst Policies In Effect." Senate Bill 104, the "Protect All Students Act," was signed by Governor Mike DeWine on 27 November 2024 and took effect 25 February 2025. It requires every K-12 school and every college and university, public and private, to designate bathrooms, locker rooms, changing and shower rooms and overnight accommodations for exclusive male or female use based on sex assigned at or near birth, and requires students to use facilities matching their birth certificate. Single-occupancy restrooms with controlled use are exempt. It was signed out of public view over objections of Democrats, teachers' unions and civil rights groups, sponsored by Republican state Senator Jerry Cirino, and contains no enforcement mechanism. Amendment of gender marker on an Ohio birth certificate was barred under the 1987 precedent In re Ladrach, challenged by four transgender Ohioans in March 2018 and invalidated as unconstitutional by federal Judge Michael H. Watson in Ray v. McCloud in December 2020. Corrections have been permitted since 1 June 2021, although some counties continue to refuse them. Name and gender on Ohio driver's licences can be changed by court order with a Declaration of Gender Change signed by a physician, nurse practitioner, social worker, therapist or psychologist, and an X marker has been available since April 2022. In August 2026 the Bureau of Motor Vehicles announced rules allowing only male or female markers and requiring an exact-matching birth certificate or passport. HB68, the Saving Adolescents from Experimentation Act, bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s and bars transgender girls and women from women's high-school and college sports. It passed on 13 December 2023, was vetoed by Governor DeWine on 29 December 2023, and was enacted by House override on 10 January 2024 and Senate override on 24 January 2024. A court blocked it in April 2024, allowed it to take effect in August 2024 after finding regulation of transgender individuals a legitimate state interest, and the Ohio 10th District Court of Appeals re-enjoined it on 18 March 2025, with Attorney General Dave Yost vowing to appeal. Ohio statutes do not address discrimination on account of gender identity, but gender-identity discrimination in state employment has been barred by executive order since 19 December 2018, and the Sixth Circuit held on 7 March 2018 that discrimination on basis of transgender status is sex discrimination under Title VII. Thirty-three Ohio cities and counties have ordinances barring gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations.

name: Iowa
text: Iowa law operates alongside United States federal law; the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Gender identity has been removed from Iowa's civil rights statutes. The state had prohibited discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing and public accommodations since 2007; in February 2025 the Legislature passed a veto-proof bill removing that category, and Governor Kim Reynolds signed it with effect from 1 July 2025. Iowa became the first state to withdraw anti-discrimination protection from a group that already held it. A 2026 law then barred localities from maintaining civil rights protections stronger or broader than the state's, after several cities passed their own ordinances, with the capital city's protections dating to 1991. A transgender visitor who is refused service, denied housing or dismissed from a job in Iowa has no state-law remedy on the ground of gender identity.

name: Florida
text: Florida stands under the United States national framework and adds a state layer a trans visitor meets directly on the ground, most sharply in public facilities. Under the Facility Requirements Based on Sex Act (Fla. Stat. 553.865), in force since 1 July 2023, a trans person may not use a restroom or changing facility consistent with their gender identity in buildings owned or leased by the state or local government: state offices, courthouses, legislative offices, prisons and jails, local immigration detention facilities, state parks, toll-road plazas, state schools, state universities, beaches and airports. The statute purports to cover all schools, public and private. Private businesses are outside its scope. The statute's mechanics put the decision with an authority figure on site. Gender labels are required, an internal disciplinary procedure applies, and an authority figure may order a person to depart; a non-member who does not leave can be charged with criminal trespass. The ACLU of Florida advises that refusing to leave a sex-segregated restroom or changing facility can amount to criminal trespass and that each situation calls for fact-specific judgment and legal counsel. There is one documented arrest. Marcy Rheintgen, a 20-year-old trans college student, was charged on 19 March 2025 after police, alerted in advance, arrested her washing her hands in a women's restroom at the Florida State Capitol, where she had declared "I am here to break the law" on entering. The misdemeanor trespass charge carried up to 60 days in jail and was described as the first arrest under Florida's transgender bathroom restrictions. On 20 June 2025 Leon County Judge Lashawn Riggans threw the case out: as a defendant charged under the statute she had no standing to argue that the law itself was illegitimate, so the statute was never substantively tested. No later arrest under the law is documented in this record. The restriction reaches higher education through administrative rulings. On 23 August 2023 the Board of Education approved firing employees of 28 public community and state colleges who enter the forbidden bathroom, and on 18 October 2023 it voted to apply a similar restriction to private college and university buildings including student housing, with compliance proof due by 1 April 2024. The federal appellate rule moved the other way first: an August 2020 Eleventh Circuit ruling that a Ponte Vedra Beach high school violated the law by refusing a transgender student consistent restroom use was reversed in January 2023 when the court sided with the district to uphold the ban, which was codified on 17 May 2023. State identity documents diverge from what many visitors hold. In January 2024 the Department of Highway Services and Motor Vehicles stopped issuing any driver's licence bearing a gender marker different from sex assigned at birth, treating holders, users and applicants as criminally guilty of fraud, with suspension and revocation of the document. In July 2024 transgender people born in Florida could not update or change sex on birth certificates despite explicit legislation permitting it. Before that closure, an amended birth certificate required an application to amend a Florida birth record, a notarized affidavit and a physician letter confirming appropriate clinical treatment, without requiring surgery or sterilisation; after 2011 a driver's licence or ID name change required a court order alongside a physician statement. Gender-affirming care is restricted in state law, and the restrictions reach adults as well as minors. On 31 October 2022 the Medical Board required a 24-hour waiting period for adults before sexual reassignment surgery; on 4 November 2022 it approved a ban on gender-affirming healthcare for minors, effective 16 March 2023 and codified 17 May 2023, which prohibits hormone replacement therapy for transgender minors and adds adult barriers including a bar on insurance coverage and a requirement that treatment be administered by a physician rather than a nurse practitioner. Minors under 18 cannot receive puberty blockers, hormone therapy or confirming surgeries unless intersex, and a board memo stated that social transition should not be a treatment option. Senate Bill 254's Physicians Only provision prohibited nurse practitioners and physician assistants from providing gender-affirming care to transgender adults, which the Human Rights Campaign reported disrupted care for an estimated 80 percent or more of transgender clinic patients, with temporary or permanent suspensions after signing. A May 2023 law allows medical practitioners to refuse treatment on grounds of conscience, religion or belief. Litigation has partly checked these rules: three plaintiffs obtained a preliminary injunction on 6 June 2023 limited to themselves, the Eleventh Circuit stayed it on 26 August 2024, and a federal judge permanently blocked provisions banning care for minors and adults in June 2024. Protection machinery at state level is thin. Florida's statutes do not address discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing or other areas, and nursing home and hospital protections in force since 2000, amended in 2007, cover sexual orientation but not gender identity. The state hate-crime law provides harsher penalties for crimes based on sexual orientation but does not cover gender identity. Since February 2021 the Florida Commission on Human Relations has announced enforcement of Bostock v. Clayton County (15 June 2020) to investigate employment, housing and public accommodations claims. Counties and cities comprising about 55 percent of the population, among them Jacksonville, Miami, Tampa, Orlando, St. Petersburg, Tallahassee and West Palm Beach, prohibit discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in private and public employment, housing and public accommodations. Two advocacy organisations have warned travellers directly. On 12 April 2023 Equality Florida took what it called the unprecedented step of issuing a travel advisory on risks to the health, safety and freedom of those considering short or long-term travel or relocation to Florida, citing laws hostile to LGBTQ people alongside reproductive-health restrictions, gun-safety rollbacks and book bans and curriculum censorship; the organisation reports events and conferences cancelling. The Human Rights Campaign joined with an updated Florida travel advisory in May 2023, citing recently signed legislation, stopping short of a boycott. Same-sex marriage has been legal in Florida since 6 January 2015, when Brenner v. Scott held the state's ban unconstitutional.

name: North Carolina
text: North Carolina sits under the United States federal framework; the national record for United States covers the federal layer. Facility rules are contested, not settled. House Bill 2, passed in an emergency 2016 session after Charlotte's council allowed transgender people to use matching facilities, required bathroom use by the sex on a birth certificate and barred city anti-discrimination ordinances covering gay and transgender people. That birth-certificate provision was repealed on 30 March 2017, and no state statute now bars a trans person from using the matching facility or criminalises facility use. Republican legislators revived a bathroom bill in the 2025 session, so the position could change. Identification documents are narrowing. A federal ruling of 26 June 2022 removed the undefined sex-reassignment-surgery requirement from the state's birth-certificate amendment process after Lambda Legal's November 2021 suit. House Bill 805, enacted over veto on 29 July 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, recognises only male and female and requires an amended certificate to keep showing the sex originally assigned alongside any change. Care for minors is closed. Three veto-overridden laws effective 16 August 2023 ended puberty blockers, hormone therapy and gender-affirming surgery to people under 18, and House Bill 574 barred individuals assigned male at birth from female sports. House Bill 805 also bars state funds for gender-transition care for minors and for people in prison, so a trans visitor in state custody would not receive transition care at state expense. A trans athlete competing in the state falls under this sports restriction. The state hate-crime statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so an assault on a trans visitor may not be charged as a bias crime even where bias is evident. Non-discrimination outside public employment is municipal and county-level. A state prohibition on local ordinances covering gender identity expired on 1 December 2020; Charlotte and Wake County ordinances covering gender identity took effect 1 January 2022, and roughly 30 per cent of the state's population lives under a local ordinance covering sexual orientation and gender identity. A trans visitor therefore has no statewide protection in private employment, housing or public accommodations, and the answer depends on the particular city or county.

name: Missouri
text: Federal protections and restrictions apply nationwide, the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Missouri's Save Adolescents from Experimentation (SAFE) Act, enacted in 2023 as Senate Bill 49, has been in force since 28 August 2023. It bars under-18 initiation of hormones or puberty blockers while allowing those already in treatment to continue, and bans all transition-related surgery for minors. A state judge denied a preliminary injunction on 29 August 2023 and the statute took effect on schedule. The same law bars MO HealthNet from paying for gender-affirming care for a patient of any age, restricts treatment in prisons, jails and correctional centres, and exposes violating providers to loss of Missouri medical licence and to lawsuits up to 15 years after treatment. Litigation began with a complaint filed 25 July 2023 in Cole County Circuit Court by Lambda Legal, the ACLU of Missouri and Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner for three families of transgender young people, medical providers, PFLAG National and GLMA. After trial in September 2024, Judge Robert Craig Carter upheld the ban on 25 November 2024 and plaintiffs announced an appeal. The Missouri Supreme Court affirmed unanimously on 13 January 2026, quoting the 2025 U.S. Supreme Court ruling upholding Tennessee's comparable ban. The statute sunsets in 2027, lawmakers state they want it permanent, and a November 2026 ballot initiative seeks to bar such care indefinitely. Governor Mike Kehoe signed HB 2009, effective 2 July 2026, providing no funds shall be expended for any cross-sex hormones or gender transition surgery for gender transition, with no taper plan for inmates already receiving care. Missouri became the seventh state to deny such care to incarcerated people and the second in 2026 to do so. Senate Bill 39, signed 7 June 2023, restricts sports in public and private schools through college to sex assigned at birth, with automatic repeal on 28 August 2027. A birth certificate sex change requires a court order with certified proof on hospital letterhead signed by the attending physician with licence and contact details stating physical sex has been altered and surgical changes are irreversible under Mo. Ann. Stat. § 193.215(9). Two 2013 cases permitting an exception were invalidated and reversed in May 2022, leaving no route around the surgical requirement. The Department of Revenue accepted Form 5532 for licence or ID gender designation after policy review between 2016 and 2024, then reverted to requiring surgery documentation or a court order after an unspecified incident. Missouri hate crime statutes explicitly cover gender identity, defined as having a self-image or identity not traditionally associated with one's gender, while state non-discrimination legislation does not address gender identity at all.

name: Alaska
text: The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Alaska is Moderate-Risk in Erin In The Morning's July 2026 assessment alongside Kentucky and North Carolina. No statewide statute bars transgender adults from restrooms or changing rooms matching gender identity or bans adult gender-affirming care, with pressure via appointed boards not legislature. Gov. Mike Dunleavy's student facility limit failed, while his appointees restricted transgender girls in girls' sports. The Dunleavy-appointed State Medical Board voted unanimously on 22 August 2025 approving draft regulation proposed June 2025 making gender-transition care to anyone under 18 unprofessional conduct risking discipline, pending Alaska Department of Law vetting and 30-day public comment. The Alaska Board of Education voted 7-1 in September 2023 to bar transgender students from female sports statewide, with facilities policy district by district. Matanuska-Susitna Borough School District voted 5-1 on 19 October 2022 for bathrooms matching sex assigned at birth or private alternative, replacing guidance standing more than seven years, an apparent first for Alaska, binding one district not adult facilities. Statewide law omits gender identity in employment, housing and public accommodations, and the 2002 executive order covers sexual orientation only for state employees. Anchorage, Juneau, Sitka and Ketchikan, about 46% of population, ban gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations, with Ketchikan passed unanimously July 2020 effective mid-August 2020. Anchorage ordinance passed 9-2 in September 2015 and survived repeal on 3 April 2018 when voters rejected Proposition 1 by 53% to 47%, which would have required bathrooms matching sex assigned at birth. In Fairbanks a February 2019 City Council ordinance on gender identity in employment, housing and public accommodations was vetoed by Mayor Jim Matherly. The hate-crime statute omits gender identity with no state enhancement, and outside the four municipalities there is no state or municipal recourse for hotel, restaurant or workplace discrimination. Amended birth certificate needs Request Form, ID photocopy, provider letter attesting appropriate clinical treatment or certified court order for change of sex, plus fee, retaining previous legal name with former-name amendment notation. Driver's licence marker change needs licensed provider letter or updated birth certificate or court order. Marriage licences issued regardless of spouses' sex since 13 October 2014 after Hamby v. Parnell voided bans, after 1996 statutory ban without Gov. Tony Knowles' signature and amendment passed 3 November 1998. Private adult consensual sex is legal, with sodomy repealed effective 1 January 1980, after the 1899 law punished crime against nature with up to ten years in prison.

name: Georgia
text: The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Senate Bill 140, signed by Brian Kemp on 23 March 2023 and in force since 1 July 2023, bars licensed medical professionals from providing hormone therapy or surgery for gender transition to patients under 18. Licence revocation is possible. Minors who began hormone replacement therapy before 1 July 2023 may continue under the law. The ACLU of Georgia said it would sue. A settlement announced in October 2023 in federal court in Atlanta requires Georgia's State Health Benefit Plan to pay for medically necessary gender-affirming care for employees, their spouses and their dependents, after a December 2022 lawsuit alleged the plan illegally discriminated by refusing to pay. The plan can cover minors' care obtained outside Georgia, even though that care is prohibited inside the state, keeping public-employee coverage alongside the 2023 ban. Atlanta police said in April 2023 that they were investigating three violent crimes against transgender women in the city that year, after two Black transgender women were fatally shot a week apart; a January 2023 shooting that left a transgender woman in critical condition also remained open. The department described the violence against Black and Brown transgender women as epidemic-level. The sourcing gives raw counts without a denominator for the city's general homicide rate, so the figures establish that these attacks occurred and were under investigation, not a risk measurably above the background rate. Memorial Health University Medical Center in Savannah cancelled all gender-affirming surgeries on 13 February 2025, including a pre-approved double mastectomy for a 24-year-old transgender man. The hospital cited following state and federal laws and regulations. Savannah Pride Center said at least two other area residents were denied care.

name: New Hampshire
text: New Hampshire is a state of the United States. The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. State law has covered gender identity in housing, employment and public accommodations since June 2018, extended to public schools effective 17 September 2019 and to health care, public accommodations and jury selection effective 1 January 2020, with anti-bullying law covering gender identity and expression including cyberbullying. Sexual orientation has been protected in public accommodations, housing and private and public employment since 1998. Hate-crime enhancements for offences motivated by gender identity took effect on 15 October 2019; sexual orientation has been covered since 1991. The gay and trans panic defence was abolished effective 1 January 2024, following passage in June 2023. On 17 July 2026 the Merrimack County Superior Court found a Concord man violated the New Hampshire Civil Rights Act by striking a transgender woman. GLAAD's 2025 census recorded 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in New Hampshire, the second-highest raw count after California (198) and ahead of Texas (66), Ohio (50) and Washington (50). The census ranks by raw count with no per-capita denominator, so the figure does not by itself establish the rate relative to larger states. A birth certificate can be changed only on proof of sex reassignment surgery, legal since 1990, with a certified court order stating a "sex change," application form, photograph and fees. A reform bill was vetoed in July 2019 and the surgical requirement remains. Driver's licences have offered male, female and X markers since 1 January 2020, implemented in August 2021; X is not available on birth certificates. Laws passed on 18 July 2024 banned gender-affirming medicine for minors and, from 1 January 2025, banned reassignment surgery for transgender minors while retaining it for intersex people and circumcisions. House Bill 377 and House Bill 712, passed in August 2025 and effective January 2026, ban puberty blockers, hormone therapy and chest surgery for under-18 care, with a grandfather clause for treatment under way as of 1 January 2026, disciplinary action against violating providers, and a right to sue. Those August 2025 laws removed access even where a physician judged it medically necessary. The same July 2024 package barred transgender girls from girls' sports in grades 5 to 12 from 19 August 2024, requiring a birth certificate for eligibility. A fourth bill in that package permitting discrimination against transgender people including adults was vetoed. In August 2024 the state Supreme Court ruled 3-1 to protect transgender students on privacy and autonomy grounds, and a judge granted a temporary stay of the sports ban pending investigation and appeals. Same-sex marriage has been legal since 1 January 2010, following civil unions from 1 January 2008. An April 2021 Supreme Court ruling recognised adultery in such marriages, reversing the 2003 Blanchflower rule. Same-sex sexual activity has been legal since the sodomy repeal of June 1975. The age of consent is 16 regardless of sexual orientation, and 18 where one party is under the care, guardianship or authority of the other.

name: Virginia
text: Virginia operates under United States federal law, and the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. The Virginia Values Act passed 6 February 2020, signed 11 April 2020 and effective 1 July 2020, bans gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing, public accommodations and credit, covers sexual orientation on same terms, and replaced state-employment-only protections. Law signed 4 March 2020 with same effective date authorises local sexual-orientation and gender-identity protections. Hate crime law covers gender-identity violence under legislation signed 4 March 2020 effective 1 July 2020, also adding sexual orientation. HB 2132 repealing gay and trans panic defence passed in March 2021, signed by Governor Northam, effective 1 July 2021. X marker on licences since 1 July 2020, and since 1 September 2020 birth certificate change needs only appropriate clinical treatment, replacing surgery requirement since 1979. §18. 2-361 struck down on 12 March 2013 and revised to decriminalise consensual same-sex relations, Senate 40-0 on 7 February 2014, House 100-0 on 6 March 2014, with immediate effect. §18. 2-345 repealed in 2013 and §18. 2-344 repealed on 4 March 2020, unenforceable since Lawrence v. Texas in 2003. Same-sex marriage since 6 October 2014, when U. S. Supreme Court declined Bostic v. Rainey/Schaefer appeal and marriages began at 1 p. m. that day. Ban repealed on 3 March 2020, protection signed in March 2024 effective 1 July, while 2006 ban remains with repeal resolutions approved in January 2025 and January 2026 awaiting voter referendum. Visitor statute signed 26 March 2007 effective 1 July 2007 extended hospital visitation to same-sex couples. In 2014 a Gloucester County school board was held to have acted unlawfully in denying a transgender high school student use of the boys bathroom, a ruling the U.S. Supreme Court allowed to stand in 2021. In July 2023 the state Department of Education adopted policies banning bathroom access and pronoun usage for transgender students, intended to be reversed in 2026. The Virginia High School League barred transgender athletes from girls sports in February 2025. Virginia prohibits health care providers from attempting to change the gender identity of minors. In September 2021 the Virginia Supreme Court upheld reinstatement of a teacher suspended for speaking against transgender children and declining to use their pronouns on grounds of Christian belief. In May 2024 Governor Youngkin vetoed a bullying-definition bill that would have included gender identity. A July 2026 legal risk assessment places Virginia in its Low-Risk States group alongside Arizona, Delaware, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and the District of Columbia, and names Virginia and Arizona as states with youth-targeting anti-trans policies which on that assessment reading of state-specific factors appear unlikely to extend to adults.

name: District of Columbia
text: The District of Columbia stands under the national framework of the United States; the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. The District has no bathroom ban of its own; the facilities restriction in force there was attached by Congress, and on 5 December 2024 transgender-rights activists protesting that measure at the Capitol were arrested. The ban originates with Congress rather than with the District's elected legislature, so it is not something the local council can repeal. A July 2026 legal risk assessment places the District of Columbia on its low-risk list alongside Arizona, Delaware, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, Virginia and Wisconsin, while cautioning that the District may no longer warrant its reputation as the most protective jurisdiction, because its law can be overridden by congressional action and by executive orders.

name: Maine
text: The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Maine law prohibits discrimination on the basis of actual or perceived gender identity or expression in employment, housing, credit, public accommodations and education opportunity. The protections were added in 2005 and retained after a veto referendum on 8 November 2005, and LD 1688, signed on 17 June 2021, wrote gender identity explicitly into state statutes. The state hate-crime law provides penalty enhancements for offences motivated by actual or perceived gender identity, and the gay and trans panic defence was abolished by legislation passed in June 2019 by 132-1 in the House and 35-0 in the Senate, effective 1 July 2019. Gender markers on Maine driver's licences and state identification cards can be changed without medical provider certification, a rule in place since November 2019, on a completed Gender Designation Form offering male, female and X options. Birth certificates reflecting gender identity, including an X marker, have been issued since July 2020 on notarized affidavit. The X marker on a birth certificate requires a declaration from a licensed physician or mental health provider, and applicants who are minors require parental consent. Maine has no state law restricting transgender people's use of sex-segregated facilities. The Maine Supreme Court ruled in January 2014 in Doe v. Regional School Unit 26 against a school district that had denied a student use of the bathroom aligned with her gender identity. A law effective since July 2023 allows 16 and 17 year olds to obtain hormone therapy as gender-affirming care, and an April 2024 law explicitly protects, defends and safeguards gender-affirming healthcare. From 1 October 2026 healthcare facilities in Maine must mandate and include sexual orientation and gender identity data. In June 2025 the Maine Senate rejected Legislative Document 233, which would have barred transgender women from competing in women's sports in state-funded schools. It was the only one of eight anti-trans bills introduced in the state in 2025 to pass the House. The University of Maine System announced on 21 March 2025, with an update on 24 March, that it would comply with federal restrictions on transgender sports participation. The announcement followed the US Department of Agriculture's suspension of federal funding for research and programmes while it investigated possible sex-based discrimination in federally funded education programmes. A July 2026 national anti-trans legal risk assessment places Maine in its Low-Risk States group. The same assessment separately flags that Maine's risk has increased because of the University of Maine System's capitulation on sports participation.

name: Delaware
text: Delaware stands under the United States federal framework. See the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. A July 2026 national assessment places Delaware in its Low-Risk States group, defined as largely refraining from targeting transgender adults without specialising in protection. Delaware has no ban on transgender bathroom and facility use according to gender identity, with the Movement Advancement Project recording no such restriction. Since 2013 under SB 97 Delaware prohibits discrimination on actual or perceived gender identity in employment, housing, public accommodations and other areas. The bill passed the Senate 11-7 on 6 June 2013, passed the House 24-17 with amendments, passed the Senate on amendments 11-9 on 18 June, was signed the next day and took effect immediately. Since 2013 Delaware adds penalties for violent crime motivated by actual or perceived gender identity. HB142 to repeal the common-law gay and trans panic defence was introduced in May 2023 and passed both houses in June 2023, with the Governor recorded as neither signed nor vetoed. Delaware allows change of legal gender marker on state ID on signed statement of a licensed medical provider alone. Since 11 February 2017 sex reassignment surgery has not been an explicit requirement for an amended birth certificate, which requires a signed affidavit of surgical, hormonal, psychological or other treatment appropriate for gender transition. As of April 2020 Delaware did not offer a gender X marker on driver's licences. Same-sex marriage has been legal since 1 July 2013, with civil unions converted to marriages. Protection machinery includes an Executive Order of 11 August 2009 for state employees and applicants on gender identity, and an Executive Order signed in January 2025 by Governor Hall-Long creating Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission.

name: Pennsylvania
text: The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Pennsylvania was low-risk tier in July 2026 anti-trans legal-risk assessment. Since June 2023 gender identity and sexual orientation discrimination banned, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Allentown, Erie, Reading keep bans. Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission covers gender identity under Human Relations Act sex ban since August 2018, with stop orders, training, economic damages. December 2022 regulations define sex to include gender identity. State employees protected since 2003, contractors since 7 April 2016. House Bill 300 passed House 102-98 in April 2023, awaits Senate vote. Since August 2016 birth certificate change on physician note of clinical treatment, no surgery, parental request below age 18, no X option. Licences/IDs offer X alongside M and F since 23 July 2020. November 2019 Philadelphia ordinances cover trans, nonbinary, gender-nonconforming youth, require at least one gender-neutral bathroom in every city-owned building and nonbinary/gender-fluid cover under Fair Practice Ordinance. December 2021 X added in all virtual public schools alongside male and female. On 17 October 2023 Mayor Jim Kenney declared Philadelphia sanctuary for gender-affirming care, barring city resources to investigate/punish in-state/out-of-state seekers, deprioritising state/federal enforcement, shielding travellers from out-of-state enforcement. Gender-affirming surgery lawful in Pennsylvania, no statewide prohibition for adults in sources reviewed. Anti-LGBTQ bias violence outside hate-crime statute, 2002 LGBTQ law struck down in 2008 as content inserted into agricultural terrorism bill, reinstatement bills never left committee. April 2021 Pittsburgh mayoral proposal sought ordinance naming gender identity, no enactment followed. Sport limits moved without becoming law. June 2022 public K-12/college male/female/coed bill restricting female teams to athletes assigned female at birth passed both chambers, vetoed 11 July 2022 by Gov. Tom Wolf. Senate Bill 9, Save Women's Sports Act, reserving women's teams for biological females in K-12/collegiate sport approved 6 May 2025, sent to House. Senate Bill 1293 under same title passed 22 April 2026, Gov. Josh Shapiro called supporters extremists, House action unclear, all concern youth school sport not transgender adults or public facility access. Consensual same-sex sexual activity legal, sodomy law held unconstitutional in 1980 Commonwealth v. Bonadio on equal protection, remaining laws repealed in 1995. Same-sex marriage recognised since Whitewood v. Wolf struck ban on 20 May 2014, before no marriages, civil unions or domestic partnerships recognised. Philadelphia offers life partnerships for long-term committed couples with city nexus, Pittsburgh provides domestic partnerships, Luzerne County defines domestic partnership as between people of same gender.

name: Michigan
text: Federal law provides the nationwide baseline for travel. The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. The July 2026 anti-trans legal risk assessment map places Michigan in its 'Low-Risk States' tier, describing the state as having enacted fairly robust non-discrimination policies while falling short on healthcare equity and on protections for incarcerated transgender people. Discrimination on the basis of gender identity is unlawful under the Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act, following a July 2022 Michigan Supreme Court ruling affirming the Attorney General's appeal, codified in a bill passed in March 2023 and signed by Governor Gretchen Whitmer on 8 March 2023. The ruling built on a 21 May 2018 Civil Rights Commission interpretation adopted 5-0 and the 7 March 2018 Sixth Circuit decision in EEOC v. R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes on Title VII. Sexual-orientation protection followed the same route, from a December 2003 executive order and a March 2013 marina-loan provision through the May 2018 interpretation to the March 2023 codification. Hate-crime law covers gender identity implicitly within the 1992 statute under 'gender', per an August 2021 declaration. A package adding 'gender identity or expression' passed the House in June 2023 and the Senate in December 2024, was signed in January 2025 and took effect 90 days after signature. Sexual orientation has been recognised for data collection since 1992. The gay and trans panic defence was abolished by law passed, signed and implemented in July 2024. Conversion therapy is banned statewide under a bill passed in June 2023 and signed in July 2023, following a June 2021 order barring taxpayer dollars or funding for minors. Birth certificate sex can be changed without surgery under a 30 June 2021 ruling declaring the 1978 surgery and physician-statement requirement unconstitutional, codified by a bill passed in December 2024. Licence or state ID change requires a signed declaration and fee since November 2019. Same-sex marriage is legal under Obergefell v. Hodges (26 June 2015), after a 1995 statute signed by Governor Engler and 2004 Proposal 04-2 approved with 58.6% barring marriage and civil unions. In DeBoer v. Snyder the ban was held unconstitutional on 21 March 2014, more than 300 licences were issued on 22 March 2014 before stays, and the Sixth Circuit reversed on 6 November 2014. The sodomy statute is unrepealed though same-sex activity is legal under Lawrence v. Texas (2003). It applied to both homosexual and heterosexual conduct, and Michigan and Massachusetts are the only northern states without codification. The Michigan Supreme Court announced a September 2023 decision on respecting pronouns for judges.

name: Nevada
text: Federal rules apply here, the national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. July 2026 assessment places Nevada in Low-Risk group, crediting robust non-discrimination policies but finding shortfall on healthcare equity and protections for incarcerated transgender people. State law bans discrimination based on gender identity or expression in employment, housing and public accommodation under provisions effective 1 October 2011 and extended throughout statutes effective 1 July 2017. In November 2022 voters approved Question 1 by 58%, adding sexual orientation and gender identity or expression to the Constitution's equal protection clause. Hate-crime law provides penalties for crimes motivated by actual or perceived characteristics, amended to add gender identity or expression after passage in May 2013, effective 1 October 2013, with reporting hotline established in January 2025. Documents can be changed without surgery. Since 2016 Vital Records issues corrected birth certificate on two affidavits reflecting preferred gender, with same for driver's licences and state IDs. DMV and Vital Records offer X designation on licences, birth certificates and state IDs with no medical documentation required, available from 2019. Legislation signed 22 June 2017 abolished 1988 requirement to publish names in newspapers before legal sex change on government documents. State law bars insurers from discriminating against transgender patients, Medicaid announced in March 2018 it would cover sex reassignment surgery, and bill passed in June 2023 and signed by the governor requires insurers including Medicaid to cover all medically necessary gender-affirming treatments effective 1 January 2024. Governor vetoed SB 302 omnibus in 2023, which would have shielded gender-affirming care and mandated Medicaid surgery coverage. In May 2023 governor approved legislation protecting transgender and intersex people in state correctional facilities. Same-sex marriage legal since 8 October 2014, when Ninth Circuit struck down ban in Sevcik v. Sandoval, with constitutional ban removed by Question 2 with 62% in November 2020 and retroactive recognition of pre-2014 out-of-state marriages required by Nevada Supreme Court in December 2020.

name: Maryland
text: Maryland is under United States federal law. The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. The Fairness for All Marylanders Act of 2014, effective 1 October 2014, bans gender identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations statewide; previously only Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Hyattsville and Montgomery County were protected. Sexual orientation discrimination is banned statewide under the Antidiscrimination Act of 2001, effective 21 November 2001. The hate-crime statute adds penalties for crimes motivated by actual or perceived gender identity, listed separately by amendment effective 1 October 2021. HB231, effective the same date, abolished the common-law gay and trans panic defence. The 2024 sanctuary law for transgender protection passed Senate 33-13 and House 97-38, signed by Governor Wes Moore, effective 1 October 2024, after a June 2023 executive order on gender-affirming healthcare access and an insurance law effective 1 January 2024 ranked most transgender healthcare friendly in the United States. Birth-certificate marker change is allowed since 1 October 2015 without surgery or sterilisation on licensed provider certification of gender identity, with X unavailable as of 2023. Motor Vehicle Administration IDs and voter registration allow X since 1 October 2019 without legal or medical documentation, with University of Maryland to add X in 2026. HB39, effective 1 October 2021, repealed the 1971 newspaper publication requirement for birth-certificate name change. In March 2018 a federal court allowed transgender student restroom and locker room use by gender identity, striking a Talbot County policy, while Montgomery County required gender-neutral bathrooms by 9-0 vote in July 2022 and Baltimore does so by ordinance. A February 2022 county report allows transgender athlete participation by gender identity without proof, documentation, or medical or legal transition, after 2022 and 2023 biological-sex team bills failed. On 11 September 2026 Sophie Lee, a 27-year-old Black trans woman, was found shot in Baltimore's Charles Village and died, the second Black trans woman shot to death in Baltimore within ten weeks. Montgomery County passed an October 2020 LGBTIQ+ bill of rights ordinance, HB130 created a 15-member Commission on LGBTIQ+ Affairs effective October 2021 expanded to 21 members in April 2023, and HB1380, effective 1 October 2022, restores honorable discharges to LGBT individuals who lived in Maryland at the time. Same-sex marriage is legal since 1 January 2013 under the Civil Marriage Protection Act, approved 72-67 in the House on 17 February 2012 and 25-22 in the Senate on 23 February 2012, signed 1 March 2012 and approved by 52.4% of voters on 6 November 2012 after a 1973 ban, with domestic partnerships since 2008 and out-of-state marriages recognised since 2010. A trans visitor whose relationship Maryland law reads as same-sex under birth-sex status can marry here.

name: California
text: California's care-access law is the most protective element of its own record. Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 107 in September 2022, making California the first state to declare itself a sanctuary for transgender young people seeking medical care. Out-of-state youth can obtain hormones and puberty blockers in California, and the law shields families from child-abuse investigations or criminal prosecution for seeking gender-affirming care, including families who travel to California for it. California's prison system is the one documented instance of identity-based placement in this inventory. As of January 2021 California is coded as the single state allowing transgender inmates to be housed according to their gender identity, with housing assigned identity-based within the general population and no trans-only separate facility documented. In 2015 California became the first state to fund gender-affirming surgeries for transgender prison inmates, and KPBS coverage of the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation's operational guidelines that year confirms the identity-based care and guidance posture while containing no explicit statement of a trans-only unit or segregation practice. The most recent documented statement of this housing practice in this record is dated January 2021; no later instance is documented. Recorded hostility sits alongside that protective framework. The GLAAD ALERT Desk documented more than 1,000 anti-LGBTQ incidents nationwide in 2025, of which California recorded 198, the highest figure of any state. That ranking is by raw count only: the source supplies no population or per-capita denominator, so the count does not establish that California is riskier for an individual visitor than a smaller state. A separate analysis of the same 2025 incident data reports a dramatic increase in anti-LGBTQ hate-crime reports in Los Angeles in law-enforcement data covering the same period as Governor Gavin Newsom's platforming of anti-trans figures. A July 2026 analysis places California in the "Safest States" law band with a score of 4.1 and 1.9 recorded incidents, and argues that even the most protective statutory floors do not eliminate recorded hostility.

name: California
text: The national record for United States covers the federal layer in detail. Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 107 in September 2022, making California the first state to declare itself a sanctuary for transgender young people seeking medical care. Out-of-state youth can obtain hormones and puberty blockers in California, and the law shields families including those who travel to California from child-abuse investigations or criminal prosecution for seeking gender-affirming care. As of January 2021 California is coded as the single state allowing transgender inmates to be housed according to their gender identity, identity-based within the general population with no trans-only separate facility documented. In 2015 California became the first state to fund gender-affirming surgeries for transgender prison inmates, and KPBS coverage of California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation guidelines that year confirms the identity-based care posture with no explicit statement of a trans-only unit or segregation practice.
